reviews.text: Their expertise and kindness are their strong points! Thank you so much for what you did for my Pepe.
I found what I was looking for in a very difficult time. Great professionalism and empathy.

Wednesday, September 23, 2026... Urgent spinal CT scan. The worst of diagnoses and the most dire of prognosis. My thanks to Dr. Riccardo Romano, who with professionalism, empathy, and his kind eyes, accompanied our big dog Goliath, sharing with us the most painful decision of our lives.

I have two dogs, and unfortunately the older one (12 years old) but smaller in size has had serious problems. On June 6, 2026, within 20 minutes, he became quadriplegic, only moving his eyes. He was immediately taken to this clinic, examined immediately, MRI, tests, etc., with the result: C3-C4 cervical hernia. On June 9, he underwent surgery and returned home a week later. The neurologist who performed the surgery, Dr. Valentino Tanga, is exceptionally skilled, professional, competent, and compassionate. The nursing staff is exceptional: helpful, professional, and attentive, supporting anxious owners, devastated by grief and the fear of losing their furry loves. The facilities are spotless, with state-of-the-art equipment. I read that someone wrote that the prices are not low. I must say that when it comes to my dog's illness (I repeat: I have two), I don't care about the price, as long as he gets better or we can get an appropriate treatment. My dog ​​is now walking again, and when I go for a checkup, Dr. Tanga is delighted with the results. Would I recommend this clinic, which is also open 24/7? Absolutely, for all the reasons mentioned above.
Excellent structure and competent staff

I wanted to leave a positive comment for the very young and highly trained doctor Gaia, who welcomed us promptly this evening, reassuring us immediately and examining my dachshund particularly thoroughly.
They helped me a lot

If you can, avoid this facility. Not so much for the service itself, but for the profoundly inhumane and cynical treatment you would receive from the same doctors.
After we brought a Cane Corso there (on August 3rd) for a suspected hernia, after an MRI and given the diagnosis of multiple spinal tumors, they recommended euthanasia. To find yourself in a situation where you don't expect your dog to die in the space of an afternoon, and to be rushed into making a decision by the vet herself—a vet who NEVER showed the slightest sign of empathy, either during the medical history or after the tests—was simply in a hurry to close the case and get back to her Sunday at the beach...
The costs are average, but bringing our dog to that facility is
a source of great regret. All it would take is a little more empathy and respect.

We rushed to this facility for our dachshund, Stitch, who was becoming paralyzed. We found an excellent, highly trained, and above all, HUMAN staff. We can't thank you enough. We've returned home and things seem to be much better! Thanks again.
P.S. You were very clear about everything, both in the diagnosis and the costs we had to face. :-)
They saved my Coco, he's responding to treatment

We brought Aron to this clinic because he was vomiting, initially for a simple ultrasound. The scan revealed a foreign body in his intestine, and we were told he needed urgent surgery.

We were offered a CT scan to determine whether the foreign body was hard or soft, arguing that the ultrasound images weren't sufficient for surgery. We pointed out that, since it was a foreign body that needed urgent removal, surgery would be necessary regardless. At that point, we were told the images were sufficient to proceed.

At first, they also told us they didn't have a place to operate on him, but then found one at the last minute, telling us they had rescheduled another operation so they could operate on Aron.

During the first operation, we were told that the intestine was in good condition and that it wasn't necessary to remove part of it: an incision, removal of the sock, and stitching would be sufficient.

After just one day, however, we were informed of a significant abdominal leak and the need for a second operation, assuming the stitches had collapsed.

The second surgeon, different from the first, reported finding a "disastrous" situation, with a torn intestine, adhesions, and the need to remove part of it.

During the second operation, a drain was also placed to monitor the abdominal fluid. To this day, we still cannot understand why a drain was not considered after the first operation, considering that we had been told that abdominal leak was one of the main potential complications of this type of surgery.

Subsequently, we were also informed of the possibility of further intestinal perforations and other procedures were proposed, including a plasma transfusion.

We asked several times whether it was really necessary to continue or if it was time to let him go, but we were always told to continue. After the transfusion, however, Aron deteriorated further, and euthanasia was proposed.

During the first surgery, we were also advised to remove the spleen because it was considered suspicious for a possible tumor. We trusted them. The histological examination, paid for separately, ruled out any tumor.

Added to all this were the conditions in which the hospitalized animals were kept: dirty, uncomfortable, and smelly cells, which we found absolutely unacceptable.

We cannot establish any medical liability, but we can share what we experienced: a management that left us with enormous doubts, a lack of clarity, and the feeling of being continually subjected to new procedures without being able to truly understand what was happening.

Aron wasn't a number. He was part of our family.

After this experience, we absolutely cannot recommend this clinic.

We regret reading such a brief review, especially because it doesn't allow us to understand what the "excessive price" comment specifically refers to.

Furthermore, the review doesn't identify the person who left it, nor does it indicate what service was offered, on what occasion, or what their expectations were regarding the price. Without these elements, it's difficult to provide a precise and constructive response.

We would like to emphasize, however, that behind every service lies time, skills, experience, professionalism, responsibility, and hard work. Recognizing and adequately remunerating work doesn't simply mean charging a price for a service, but rather valuing the people and resources needed to offer a quality service.

We understand, of course, that a price may not meet everyone's expectations or possibilities: this is a completely legitimate assessment. Defining a price as "excessive" without providing any reference to the service received or the factors that led to such a judgment is a different matter.

We would be happy to discuss this with you should you wish to identify yourself and provide us with more details, because a concrete and transparent discussion is always more useful than an anonymous, context-free judgment.
Great professionalism. Our Mocio, who could no longer stand due to a herniated back, has been able to resume a normal life for many more wonderful years! A special thanks to Dr. Valentino Tanga.

I had already been to this clinic several years ago for my elderly dog, who was taken in from the shelter. They saved him!
I returned on Monday for my cat Nuvola. She was sick, and I was hoping for the same outcome, but unfortunately, the tests and ultrasound revealed a clinical picture that's beyond recovery, and we decided to put her to rest.
We do so much to save them from bad situations, to give them a life full of love, and it's right not to make them suffer in the end. The clinic staff is truly special, helpful with their explanations and kind with their words. A special thanks goes to Dr. Gualtieri and the vet who performed Nuvola's ultrasound (sorry, I don't remember his name). Their humanity is rare, even among human doctors.
I always recommend this clinic to everyone: it's the only one in Rome with truly competent vets, not young students left to fend for themselves.
The price is average for other clinics/veterinary emergency rooms.

Very careful with money, not very careful with communication, at least not the vet who examined my cat.
For a biopsy, I was emailed a quote for €1,030.00, but the same sample at another center cost less than half that, with a satisfactory explanation.

In April, I went to this clinic recommended by the vet who was caring for my cat, requesting an urgent CT scan because she had a fever and a liver lesion that needed further investigation.
The next day, she had a CT scan, after which it was confirmed that there was room for surgery, but the fever never went down. She remained in the clinic from Monday to Thursday. They advised me to let her stay there, but since she wasn't eating, they also agreed that it would be best to take her home to see if her appetite had returned.
The CT scan revealed a tumor mass in her liver and spleen. I asked what could be done (I would have done everything, obviously), and was told to contact a veterinary oncologist to assess the feasibility of surgery (I should have found one myself). After finding one, the oncologist, of course, told me that, since he didn't know anything about the situation, he couldn't give any advice on the matter.
Only after I asked a veterinary oncologist who worked with them to ask them myself was I told they would ask, a response that came after my Trilly had already passed away on this earth.

Unfortunately, my Trilly died a few days after being discharged. My experience with this facility was terrible; I only found excuses to avoid the operation, beating around the bush (no metastases in other organs had been found). If you're afraid of surgery, you should say so clearly, avoiding placing an animal who was suffering in a facility.
Very professional and capable, at the same time they listen and are very helpful and attentive.

The least we can do is come in with an epileptic dog and come out with a dog who is now suffering the serious consequences of adding another drug to his regimen. The contraindications of this drug (for human use) have brought him to the brink of death. Needless to say, I don't recommend the neurology department.

I've been using the services offered by this facility for many years, and a few years ago one of my dogs underwent successful hernia surgery. Unfortunately, something has changed recently; I was even advised to take one of my dogs with pus in one ear elsewhere, saying they couldn't handle it. What a shame.

The facility is always available as an emergency veterinary clinic. Efficient and competent. They saved my dog ​​several times due to emergency admissions.
Special mention goes to Dr. Valentina Papa, a neurologist who is treating Carlotta.

Terrible, AVOID THEM.
The person who greeted us, after explaining that the dog had an epileptic seizure and was in pain, dismissed us, telling us that if the dog is in pain, it will die and he can't do anything... Without even examining the dog.
This is the second time we've had an experience like this at this clinic....
Terrible in every way. They're unfit to work.
Go elsewhere if you don't want to waste your time or your dog.

Unfortunately, our experience with this clinic was profoundly negative.

We turned to them for a dog that needed careful attention, and from what we experienced, we felt they had been handled in a sloppy and inaccurate manner, especially considering the situation and how quickly it deteriorated.

Just a day and a half after that visit, that dog is no longer with us.

Unfortunately, we carry with us the feeling that the situation was not assessed with the depth and attention it deserved.

When you take your pet to a veterinarian, especially when he's ill, you put your trust in their expertise completely and expect thoroughness, attention, and the utmost caution. In hindsight, we would have liked to see all of this in much greater measure.

Today, unfortunately, there remains enormous pain and many questions about those final hours that will never be given a second chance.
I have known this clinic for a long time and am more than satisfied with it, as are several Canarian friends.
I felt very comfortable with all the staff, compliments to Dr. Simona Palermo. I recommend her both for the honesty of the process and the professionals. Everything is very clear.
Terminally ill cat cared for with care and expertise
Super professional. Excellent experience.
Very satisfactory neurological visit

Good morning, my experience with the Etiopia Clinic was positive. I brought my cat Stella for observation after a terrible respiratory crisis, which was urgently managed by my vet, who saved the cat. She recommended this clinic to me to continue monitoring the cat and possibly administer oxygen therapy, which fortunately was not necessary. I must say they were kind, both at the time of admission, with a doctor who greeted the cat and explained the treatments they would be giving her, and especially at discharge with Dr. Colombo, who was very kind and attentive. She recommended all the treatments we needed to improve the life of our cat with this serious lung problem. I must say that, unlike other clinics I've worked with, I was very satisfied. The facility is a bit dated, but the important thing is the medical team and the empathy, in my opinion. Obviously I hope I never need them again, but if I do, I would definitely return. Thanks to Dr. Colombo.
Attentive, thorough, kind, professional, and thorough. Despite the unpleasant nature of the visit, it was a great experience. I recommend them to anyone who needs them.
Excellent, perfect for the experience demonstrated, THANK YOU.
Excellent experience. I went there for a specialist appointment (neurology) at the recommendation of my dog's vet. They were thorough, competent, and attentive.
excellent from 2022 to today...

Today, a holiday, I brought in a 14-year-old cat with a devastating medical condition. Therefore, a case of euthanasia. It wasn't an easy task, but in addition to waiting almost two hours, the doctor on duty (only one to manage an entire clinic with dozens of cases) was in great difficulty. Unfortunately, not being very experienced and not even having the support of a nurse, she had to perform the euthanasia, making a series of mistakes that made the situation even more complicated. If the person who was with me hadn't helped her, I really don't know how the situation would have ended. First, she had to make several attempts to find the vein in the cat, who was dehydrated. The cat suffered and even struggled. We then urged the doctor to administer some anesthesia. One dose wasn't enough (it was obviously not the right dose), but after the second, the cat calmed down and she managed to insert the cannula, after which she administered stronger anesthesia and medication to put him to sleep forever. In short, it was truly heartbreaking. For us and for the poor cat, who was already suffering from the illnesses that had exhausted him.
What should have been a moment of peace has become an extremely difficult time.
I repeat, a clinic that leaves the care of dozens of patients to a single doctor (not particularly experienced) is a disgrace. A gross disrespect for those who have to wait for hours, whether it's an emergency or not.
We are shocked.

Always available. Dr. Papa is my irreplaceable point of reference. I have three Cavalier King Charles Spaniels, incredibly sweet and endearing dogs, but with extremely delicate health. Dr. Valentina Papa is my guarantee. I know she's always there for me and my pets. Thank you, Doctor. Ines Bianchedi

I had a great experience. My dog ​​is now in the final stages of his life. Compared to other clinics, I had immediate results and a lot of empathy. No miracles... but for those, you don't need to go to the clinic, but elsewhere :(

It's not easy to rate the Ethiopia Veterinary Clinic, because when I went there were so many people and obviously it wasn't easy for anyone to manage! What amazed me was the extreme patience of the receptionist! Otherwise, the quality of the vets is top notch! I met Dr. Papa and I think she is able to explain exactly like no other the pathology and the dog's problem. She is also a nice, kind, and welcoming person. The professionalism and top-notch organization could be improved, but I repeat, it was a truly full day, full, full, full!

We brought our cat here after an accident, and they literally saved his life. The staff is incredibly kind and competent, available 24/7 for anything. A huge thank you to everyone, from the doctors to the interns and the reception staff. You can see they do their job with dedication and passion. Thank you again.
Professionalism and courtesy. Care for both our puppies and their owners. Clean facility and excellent organization.

I brought my cat here because she had stopped eating, was vomiting, had diarrhea, and was increasingly depressed. I was repeatedly told that the top priority was getting her to eat again, but despite several days of hospitalization, a clear diagnosis was never reached, nor was there any significant improvement in her condition.
I constantly felt that the problem was being passed from one veterinarian to another, with no one truly taking responsibility for the case and attempting to reach a diagnosis. Communication between the professionals at the facility was poor, as was communication with the veterinarians who subsequently took care of my cat.
By the time I decided to transfer her to another clinic for further evaluation, it was too late. I lost my cat after days when, in my opinion, the investigation and intervention should have been quicker and more thorough.
Unfortunately, this isn't even the first traumatic experience I've had with this facility. Over the years, I've entrusted two of my pets to this clinic, and I lost both of them.
I know that veterinary medicine cannot save every patient. What I expected was professionalism, attention, communication, and a genuine desire to understand what was happening. In my experience, all of this was missing.
I will never return to this clinic, and I will not recommend it to anyone who truly cares about their animals.
Great experience...professional...

Professionalism, integrity, competence...
DJANGO, my amstaff, always welcomed with affection and helpfulness...
Attentive to your problems...and their solutions...To Dr.
Alessandro Iacozzilli, always thank you for everything...presence, experience, attention 🙏Thank you, Doctor!

Clinic with specialized staff, who are above all very kind and caring towards animals and their owners.
I had a great time; Dr. Papa was excellent with my little dog.
The facility is excellent.

Honest and competent...from what I understand...
Anyway, very kind.
Great weather. In 2020, they saved my little Phoebe from dying. The other night, I was with my Dexter for another emergency. Prompt and professional.
Friendly and helpful staff. My dog ​​was treated very well, and the vets were very helpful and thorough in their explanations. Recommended clinic.

Dr. Ilacqua was very good. During my dog's first visit, she prescribed extensive checkups and a comprehensive treatment plan, which unfortunately proved to be very expensive, complex, and unmanageable in the long term. I was waiting for a response from the doctor via email regarding the medical checkups she had prescribed, but I was told that a repeat visit was necessary at the same cost of €120 to evaluate the reports and possibly update the treatment. I have never had a specialist, after a paid visit, ask to be paid again to evaluate tests he had prescribed. I consider this process truly unusual, and unfortunately, I had to terminate the relationship that had been established.
I'd say excellent!
A reliable veterinary emergency center with friendly and efficient staff. The only drawback is the parking.
Thank you! :)

The staff immediately proved attentive, knowledgeable, helpful, and very empathetic.
They explained the situation to us carefully, with sensitivity but also clarity, highlighting the pros and cons of each option, the costs, and the potential savings of having some tests performed in an outpatient setting versus a clinic.
I hope I never need them again, but I would definitely return to them.
The helpfulness and attention we received are not a given.
Alberto Sordo thanks you.
Thank you! :)

I went for a limping problem with my staffie. We had an initial visit with the neurologist, Dr. Papa. I had an excellent first impression, very attentive and meticulous. We then had to have an MRI and everyone was very kind, friendly and attentive to the well-being of my dog. Fundamentally, they are all very humane. I can only give a super positive review.
Dr. Papà, who has been treating my cat for several years, is empathetic and professional.

Excellent veterinary clinic: my dog ​​had diagnostic tests done very quickly. The doctors are kind, helpful, and empathetic. I also really appreciated their professionalism in providing clear and helpful information over the phone.

Things don't always go the way you'd like, but in the moment of an inevitable and unexpected farewell, being there is as important as being there... thank you for everything you did to accompany our beloved Mino to the bridge with dignity and respect, and for the way you called, informed, and treated us.

Thank you to all the caring doctors, nurses, and staff.

Alessandra

Unfortunately, my experience with this veterinary clinic was extremely negative. My dog ​​received an incorrect diagnosis, which was followed by the administration of medications inappropriate for his actual condition. Once he returned home, the dog became ill due to the incorrect treatment, further aggravating the situation.
Furthermore, upon discharge, we were not provided with a clear and accurate treatment plan to follow at home, leaving us without any essential guidance for managing the problem.
Another very serious aspect concerns the conditions in which the dog was kept: dirty, surrounded by urine and feces, with no attention to hygiene or the animal's well-being. I consider this situation unacceptable for a facility that should guarantee care, professionalism, and respect.
Finally, the quotes requested were extremely high compared to the service received, which unfortunately did not live up to expectations or minimum standards of care.
I hope this review will serve to inspire reflection and improve the service, so that other animals and owners do not have to go through a similar experience.
Thank you! :)

A heartfelt thank you to the entire team at the veterinary clinic for their professionalism, promptness, and above all, the humanity you showed. Our dog arrived in desperate condition, and you welcomed him immediately, caring for him with great care and respect. You accompanied him with kindness, allowing him to pass away without suffering, in the most natural way possible. In such a difficult time, your compassion truly made a difference. We will never forget it.

Thank you so much ❤️
Excellent clinic, always friendly, helpful, and professional staff. Dr. Sara Pellone is an excellent cardiologist.
Trained, attentive and friendly staff.

Unfortunately, my experience was not positive. I perceived the facility as dated, poorly maintained, and in need of major renovation, both in terms of its facilities and overall organization. From an administrative and management perspective, I also felt inefficiency and a lack of precision.
During my experience, concerns arose regarding the medical professionalism, especially in terms of coordination, clarity, and consistency of service. The technological equipment and machinery appeared not particularly up-to-date. The external context contributed to an overall less than tasteful image. Overall, I did not perceive the level of care, reliability, and quality that I consider essential in an environment dedicated to animal health.
Thank you! :)

Thanks to Dr. Alessandro Arrighi's prompt intervention, I admitted my cat to the emergency room for a life-threatening abdominal and lung effusion. From day one, I received exceptional, professional and humane care at the clinic. I would like to emphasize the compassion and promptness of the doctors I met, providing explanations day after day, both over the phone and during visiting hours. I saw the feline ward treated extremely well, and all the kittens waiting in the same room as mine were cared for with care and attention. Today, only thanks to them, my big cat will be able to go home with the prescribed treatment, and I know that in any other emergency, I can rely on highly professional and compassionate staff. I was able to visit the cat for the entire hour and a half scheduled over three days, cuddling him and personally feeding him, and I received precise updates on his progress. Thank you so much for everything you have been able to do and continue to do every day.

I will never stop thanking the clinic staff for what they did for my Enea! I could mention everyone, but I'll just mention Dr. Mariasole Colombo and the surgical team members Doricchi and Capezzone. For their professionalism, availability, and commitment, as well as an empathy that unfortunately isn't always found. Thank you again!
Thank you! :)
They were extremely professional and helpful with an emergency with my dog
Thank you! :)

The vets and staff were all competent, helpful, and welcoming. Excellent explanations.
Thank you!

My 14-year-old dog Luce was dying thanks to the professionalism of the doctors and assistants. Thank you ❤️
from the bottom of my heart.

I can't give a positive review: the environment is unclean, the service is slow. Prices are high for the service they provide. The doctors may be good, but the information they provide about health conditions varies based on their own profit.
Yes I had a great time, thank you

As a child, my mother and I had urgently brought our dogs to this clinic and even then they were very prepared and available. Recently I brought my French bulldog and they continue to be impeccable from the welcome that was made by four people to solve the problem to the veterinary staff very attentive and caring towards the dog. They are truly super
Super doctors, great staff
ready, present, reassuring and very helpful!

I had a terrible experience with this facility. I showed up in an emergency with my dog ​​who had just fallen, clearly in need of immediate attention, but I was turned away without anyone even bothering to look at him.
I find it unacceptable that a place that calls itself a "veterinary clinic" doesn't even offer basic assistance in an emergency situation. A complete lack of empathy, professionalism, and responsibility.
I strongly advise against this facility to anyone who truly cares about their pet's health.
Abivet Exams

A rather negative experience: they turned me away from the emergency room because they were fully booked, so if the cat had been in a serious condition they wouldn't have taken him in. However, they suggested I have him checked out quickly to check the condition of his bladder. They wouldn't let me in, but after 20 seconds, someone came out and told me to take him somewhere else; he told me he probably needed to be hospitalized (which wasn't true; fortunately, the cat was later examined at Polivet and is doing fine, thankfully!!!).
Hospitality, courtesy and professionalism!
Dr. Valentino Tanga saved my 13-year-old dog who had a hernia

Unfortunately, I've known this facility for years. The "unfortunately" is because people would prefer to do without it, but if needed, at least there's a guarantee. I've always found them professional, helpful, and empathetic.

I had already had positive experiences with the clinic many years ago, so I went straight to them again with my Maltese, who had a case of poisoning with hemorrhagic colic. I found the doctors welcoming, empathetic, and clear.
Exceptional. Great expertise.

They removed a hernia in my Weimaraner a couple of years ago for an exorbitant price. The first surgery was a botch, and a few months later he had another operation because he couldn't walk properly. I paid back the full amount, but since then he's always had trouble walking and struggled to get up from a sitting position, despite extensive physical therapy. He was taken to another clinic a week ago because he couldn't walk anymore, and they confirmed they botched the surgery.
Positive experience, I operated on my dog ​​for a hernia, the surgery was difficult, but everything went well, thanks to the neurosurgeon and all the staff
Great experience! Very knowledgeable and attentive staff, completely satisfied.
The staff were friendly, knowledgeable, and helpful. They were truly comforting and extremely professional during a terrible time.

Thank you for saving Snow.
Thank you for helping me with her rehabilitation, and thank you for always being available.

The attitude of the lady at reception this morning, February 10, 2026, didn't seem appropriate to us. It didn't seem appropriate for the context. She showed signs of irritation, spoke in rather heated tones, and, in short, was quite nervous. She attacked the door of the room (where the hospitalized dogs were kept), slamming it hard, and the girl who was there.
It seemed excessive and out of place, and it didn't make a good impression. I hope action will be taken as soon as possible, after having spoken and consulted the girl (nurse, technician, or doctor) in question. There were several of us who witnessed the scene, which is not possible.
The visit, overall, went well, but if this is the attitude at the entrance, it's entirely reasonable to imagine what could happen with the dogs who won't stop crying.
I feel sorry for the lady who gets irritated by hearing the dogs and being in this context. Perhaps it would be better to listen to the noise of the supermarket checkouts; it's more bearable. Overall she was quite nice to the customers
The best veterinary clinic in Rome

I waited too long to write this review! I'm not one for reviews, but what happened here is truly disgusting. We brought our Simba (8 and a half years old) on the afternoon of Saturday, November 22nd, not for the first time, because we had noticed that something was wrong. After 5 minutes of visiting (I repeat, 5 minutes of visiting for €120), they sent him away, saying it was no big deal. We went home, but I noticed that he was getting worse, so we decided to take him back. We arrived shortly before 10 pm. The waiting room was empty! They told us to wait. I should point out that my dog ​​was obviously ill; he couldn't stand up, he was shaking, drooling, and his eyes were half-closed. After we had been waiting for more than an hour, the waiting room started to fill up. Everyone was walking past. It was 1 am and still nothing. When I asked for explanations (in an angry tone), I was told, "You already came this afternoon, if you're not happy, go somewhere else!" We wait. Meanwhile, the room is empty again. Ignored by the people who were working that night! At 3:40 in the morning, I lose my patience again and start banging my hand on the counter to make them feel like we're still there. Puff! Strangely enough, everyone comes out from behind the scenes! The first thing they say to me is, "We have to keep him here tonight/morning, we'll give you a QUOTE," without actually knowing what he really had. We ask to speak to the "director" about the terrible management of the night before, and the "director" did nothing but protect us from what had happened. He reassures us by saying that he had examined Simba, who wasn't in danger and just needed treatment. Moral of the story, do you want to know? After 4 days in there, Simba left us. I should add that the day my Simba flew away, I called around 10 in the morning asking if I could go visit him at lunchtime because for work reasons I couldn't go in the afternoon, and they told me there was no problem. If I had arrived 20 minutes later, I wouldn't have been able to say goodbye to him even for the last time. They didn't even bother to tell me that his conditions had worsened. I'll leave you to draw your own conclusions. As many have already written, when you enter there, the first thing they talk about is a QUOTE! The "ANIMALS" are not the little souls we bring you, but you! STAY AWAY! Final bill: €1,700 to leave with just the collar. SHAMEFUL.

I went to my bully for back problems... we were super pampered and they were truly professional, fast, and professional.
I highly recommend... a FABULOUS CLINIC

I highly recommend them.
The first time, on the night of Italy's victory at the European Championships, they saved my dog's life. He ended up there in the middle of the night and was able to diagnose him with a rare condition (peripheral nervous system paralysis) and guide him toward recovery, even though he was over 12 years old (he's no longer with us, but he lived for many more years thanks to them).

A second time, the following year, they saved my cat's life, also in the middle of the night, due to a very serious kidney failure.
I found great compassion, the possibility of paying in installments, and reasonable prices. They even allowed me to visit outside of their office hours, despite their high workload, understanding that my working hours weren't compatible with their visiting hours.

For emergencies, they are the absolute best.
Expertise, humanity, and kindness. The best!
My cat wasn't feeling well, they took very good care of him

On more than one occasion, I've had the opportunity to test the expertise of the clinic's doctors. Even when they couldn't solve the problem, I've found a friendly and caring environment. If they weren't just an emergency room, I'd always go there to have my furry friends treated!

I called this clinic just by looking at the reviews, and I have to say I had a great experience. I highly recommend it. Very attentive and caring. It's a shame I live in Milan, otherwise it would have become my go-to clinic. Thanks to all the staff, you're amazing.
Kind, prepared, friendly team, truly TOP. IF IT WERE POSSIBLE I WOULD GIVE IT 10 STARS. THANKS TO ALL OF YOU.
Very professional, attentive to the owners' requests. We had an excellent experience in the orthopedic department, thanks to Dr. Colaiacomo.
Very competent and empathetic staff

They helped me get an elderly cat back on her feet with an internal ear infection.
She was hospitalized for almost a week, but the nurses and veterinarians never lacked compassion during the daily visits.
Thank you so much.

P.S.
Please be very careful on the entrance road: it's dangerously poor, in terrible condition, and there's a significant risk of damaging your car if you're not careful.

Very helpful. The first time, years ago, on the night of December 26th, they saved our dog Bettina, and the cost was very reasonable and fair.
Yesterday at 11:00 PM, we called over the phone about an emergency involving our Birillo. They assisted us with great availability and courtesy, reassuring us and giving us directions on what to do.
What more can I say? Thank you 🤗 🤗 🤗 🤗
Excellent clinic! From the medical staff to the receptionists, they are always attentive to their clients' needs and, above all, professional.
Everyone was very kind, from the reception to all the healthcare staff.

The kind and attentive welcome of the staff as well as of the doctor, whose professionalism and accuracy in explaining my dog's situation convinced me to come back here for a check-up even though it is quite far away from me.
Prepared, friendly and kind
My emergencies are always at this hospital. The doctors are competent and empathetic!

Good morning everyone....unfortunately I have to agree with some of the reviews I read below....I'm not talking about the facility in general but about my experience with Dr. Papa....our dog (a French bulldog) was being treated by the doctor....I'll start by saying that the doctor has always been kind and helpful and is certainly a good person but perhaps in our case she was at least superficial....my dog ​​suffered from epileptic seizures due to her advanced age (she left us after 11 and a half years of unconditional love) the doctor had found a cure that had managed to limit my furry friend's seizures (obviously you go by trial and error especially with dosages in these cases) however in the last 2 months there had only been one morning with 2 small seizures, otherwise my little girl was lively and active as always (of course considering her age) at the September check-up the doctor changed her medication to try a different approach....in these cases you go by trial and error but since there is no drug that It can safely stop the seizures. I asked if it was worth changing since (according to the doctor herself) the drug was being taken well and the liver tests had remained at the same values ​​(high, it must be said) as before.....that is, the concern that they could get further worse wasn't arising.....the only thing is that my dog ​​was peeing a lot.....but given her age and the situation, I wondered if it was worth the risk....anyway, within 5 days of not taking the old drug, my little girl had a devastating seizure that took her away.....coincidentally, on the same day of hospitalization, we met with Dr. Papa and we talked....given that no one can predict these things, it was the doctor's response that irritated me....."evidently the new treatment isn't being assimilated but I was forced to change it"....forced by whom? (Not from the tests because even though they were high, the values ​​remained unchanged and the absorption of the old drug was good) We can make mistakes, it's human and no one is to blame for this (or doctors are doing their job) but I found it inappropriate and cowardly to put one's hands up in this way.....probably with the old treatment it would have lasted maybe 3 months, 6 months, a year, we don't know but anyone who has a dog knows that even 6 more months together are a very long time (and I underline lived well and without further suffering)..... if it hadn't been for that response, in my opinion cowardly, I wouldn't have written this post..... I still thank the facility and the staff and also Dr. Papa but the pain is so much....and we also have to admit our mistakes, we all make them but some leave us truly empty....have a good day

On the recommendation of my trusted veterinarian, I went to this clinic for an MRI scan for my cat, who had likely suffered ischemia (related to heart disease). The clinic deemed it mandatory to perform a neurological examination before the MRI, which, however, was not available in the short term despite the cat's serious condition. After about four days, an appointment was scheduled with Dr. Papa, who (after a completely inaccurate examination) deemed the MRI unnecessary. The doctor also described the cat as having "no heart disease." Finally, the neurologist concluded the examination hastily, as she herself admitted she had other personal commitments.
Shortly afterward, my cat sadly died, due to ischemia and cardiovascular problems. I don't know if he could have been saved, but treatment could certainly have been attempted if only the examination had been performed by a professional, with the necessary tests for a diagnosis. I absolutely do not recommend it.

Now, I really don't know how it's possible to speak well of these incompetent people. They're clearly poorly trained and evidently satisfied with the enormous profit they make at every opportunity. Well, this is the second time I've lost my dog ​​here in truly disconcerting circumstances. The first was due to a presumed leishmaniasis, which later turned out to be a resolvable poison intoxication. The second time was due to a small piece of plastic that caused intestinal obstruction in my Pitbull. A simple operation was unsuccessful. Furthermore, when the stitches had evidently had problems from the first operation, the surgeon didn't inform us until complications arose.
I'm writing this because I've done my utmost to inform you, and I've found that a tear in the stitches in soft tissue can only happen if there are obvious problems during the operation, and yes, if done properly, they certainly don't lead to certain consequences a few hours later.
If he had told us this first, it would have been more correct, and he would have, what for? Charity is far from solving the problem, calling another surgeon.
A surgery that goes badly in 2% of cases on a six-year-old dog in perfect health who was bursting with life.
Moreover, for the second surgery we paid 800 euros compared to the thousand for the first. It was a real disgrace.
These people are incompetent. Turn to others and be careful, because veterinary medicine is a field that is absolutely incomparable to human medicine. The lack of accountability for mistakes, as well as the generous compensation, create terrible situations.
When the affection for our animals is identical, if not superior, because it is different from that for people, even loved ones.
Please be careful, do not operate on your animals here. I beg you.
